en: Mount Mayon in Albay has a perfectly symmetrical cone shape formed by continuous, visible layers of erupted lava and ash.
The Pasig River physically connects Laguna de Bay to Manila Bay, flowing directly through the highly urbanized capital region.
Mount Pulag in Benguet features a sea of clouds phenomenon where cold air traps moisture below its high peak.
The Philippine eagle in Mindanao's forests has a distinctive, observable crest of long, shaggy, dark brown feathers.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows directly into the sea, allowing boats to navigate its dark cave.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the second-largest lake in the Philippines, serving as the visible source of the Agus River.
Tubbataha Reefs in the Sulu Sea feature massive, shallow coral atolls that provide visible habitats for hundreds of marine species.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol turn brown during the dry season because the intense sun dries the grass covering the mounds.
Callao Cave in Cagayan contains a natural chapel brightly illuminated by direct sunlight shining through a specific ceiling opening.
Maria Cristina Falls in Lanao del Norte features twin waterfalls that dramatically plunge 320 feet into a deep, rocky gorge.
The white sand of Boracay's White Beach is primarily composed of crushed coral and shells broken down by ocean waves.
Mangrove trees in Panguil Bay have specialized aerial roots that stick out of the mud to breathe in oxygen-poor soil.
